summary.text: The formal statement is merely the tautology \(\mathrm{True}\), so the proof is immediate and contains no number-theoretic argument. In particular, it does not establish the claimed obstruction to pairwise coprimality.

full_proof.text:
The proposition to be proved is simply \(\mathrm{True}\).

By definition, \(\mathrm{True}\) is the proposition that holds unconditionally: it has a canonical witness, requiring no assumptions and no subsidiary construction. Taking this witness proves \(\mathrm{True}\).

Therefore the stated theorem holds.

No assertion about four-square representations, the coefficients \(a,b,c\), or pairwise coprimality occurs in the theorem statement, so those notions play no role in this proof.
